neighbours.label: the thing claimed as one's own in 'have the whole X to ourselves' / taking a place or thing for oneself (exclusive possession)
fire: We got there at dawn and had the whole beach to ourselves for an hour.
On a Tuesday in March you can have the entire museum practically to yourself.
The two brothers wanted the farm to themselves and refused to share it with their sister.
Since the others left early, Anna had the cabin all to herself for the weekend.
The settlers were determined to keep the valley for themselves and drove off newcomers.
After the crowds went home we had the whole lake to ourselves under the stars.
The cat has claimed the sunny armchair as her own and nobody else dares sit there.
The empire wished to hold the mountain passes for itself alone.
quiet: We got there at dawn and walked the whole beach before breakfast.
On a Tuesday in March the museum offers free guided tours every hour.
The two brothers repaired the old barn on the farm with their sister.
Since the others left early, Anna cleaned the cabin before the weekend.
The settlers built a small church in the valley and planted orchards.
After the crowds went home we watched the stars reflected on the lake.
The cat sleeps in the sunny armchair most afternoons in the summer.
The empire built roads through the mountain passes to move its armies.

notes: Card: 'Felt like we had the whole trail to ourselves' (191), 'claim a bit of it as my own', 'have the island to themselves', 'desired the maiden to be his bride', 'keep Afghan territory under their influence'. Logit promotes mine/ours/for. Near misses use the same nouns without exclusive possession.
